cards.explanation: The answer is that Jesus can make him clean. The man kneels and says, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.” I think there's a lot packed into that little “…if You are willing…” He says what he believes Jesus can do and leaves the rest in Jesus' hands.

The answer is that Jesus reaches out and touches him. Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. Then He said, “I am willing… Be clean!” (Matthew 8:3) The touch comes right there with the words. Friends, I would have stood there a second just taking that in.
The answer is False. The text says, “And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.” There's no few days of waiting, friends. Jesus says the word and the healing is done.

The answer is priest. Jesus says, “But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them.” After the healing, the priest is the one He sends the man to. I'd love to have seen that priest's face, friends.

The answer is his servant. The centurion, an army officer, says, “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.” He's come to plead for someone else. I think that tells you something about how he sees his servant.
The answer is True. After the centurion tells Him about his servant, Jesus replies, “I will go and heal him…” Those are His words. He says He'll go and heal him.
The answer is having Jesus come under his roof. The centurion says, “Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.” Notice he keeps calling Jesus Lord, too.
The answer is word. The centurion says, “But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.” He isn't asking Jesus to come under his roof, friends. Just a word.

The answer is that he knows a command gets obeyed. The centurion says, “For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes.” Then he adds that his servant does what he's told. I think he's saying a word from Jesus is all it takes, because that's what he's just asked for.

The answer is that Jesus hasn't found faith this great in Israel. He says, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.” Think about that, friends. The man who gets this praise is an army officer who asked for a word.

The answer is the banquet. Jesus says many “…will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.” So the guests come from far and wide, and what they share is the banquet. A banquet is right up my alley, friends, and mine would have cookies on every plate.
The answer is believed. Jesus tells the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” It's tied to his believing, friends. His servant is healed at that very hour.

The answer is True. The text says, “And his servant was healed at that very hour.” Jesus had just told the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” The healing is recorded right after those words.

The answer is that she gets up and serves Him. The text says, “…the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve Him.” The fever leaves, and she's up on her feet. Imagine going from a sickbed to serving, friends. I can't even get off the couch after a long day of stamping.

The answer is False. The text says Jesus “…drove out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.” Every sick person brought to Him that evening was healed, friends. There's no left-behind group in that line.

The answer is the prophet Isaiah. The text says this “…was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah…” Then it quotes, “He took up our infirmities and carried our diseases.” The words are credited to the prophet Isaiah, friends.
